name: sol_basics_payment_2
description: Payable function accepts an amount parameter without verifying msg.value equals it
question: The source file in `source` defines a payable function that takes a payment `amount` parameter and uses that parameter (e.g., to credit balances, record deposits, or transfer value) without requiring `msg.value == amount` or otherwise validating that the ETH actually sent matches the specified amount, allowing a caller to under-pay or over-pay ETH while the function still records or acts on the stated `amount`. This excludes functions that do not accept ETH (non-payable) and functions that explicitly check `msg.value` against the parameter (e.g., via a require statement) before proceeding.
criteria: A payable deposit(uint256 amount) function sets balances[msg.sender] += amount without any require(msg.value == amount) check
A payable buyTokens(uint256 amount) function transfers `amount` tokens to the caller while ignoring the actual ETH received in msg.value
A payable pay(uint256 amount) function forwards `amount` to a recipient via call{value: amount} while msg.value could be less, draining contract funds
A payable fund(uint256 amount) function emits an event or updates state using `amount` parameter but never compares it to msg.value
